# STATUS

## Run Ledger - 2026-07-06 Wave 0 GitHub Convergence / Release Gate / Branch Protection

Closed Wave 0 follow-through after the July Convergence work reached GitHub. PR #66 (`goat/july-convergence`) merged to `main` as `1640557e8a0813d3cdefcf7d2446ac2e460b7c29`, bringing the July 5 snapshot and GOAT Waves 0-3 work onto GitHub. The associated GitHub Pages workflow for that convergence merge passed and deployed the July build, while main CI exposed release-gate wiring/runtime issues that were fixed in follow-up PR #67.

PR #67 (`codex/fix-release-gate-ts-test`) fixed release-gate TypeScript and browser-smoke harness failures and merged as `89c077f95634b2bf2b265f6757ddac692139d075`. The fix stayed in CI/test harness scope: TypeScript grade-season tests now run through Vitest, the release gate runs on Node 24, the release-gate timeout allows the full gate to finish, post-setup browser smokes prefer the local Vite preview binary, preview startup has separate timeout/diagnostics, preview child signal/error exits are detected, and stale full-setup smoke copy assertions were aligned to source-verified setup copy. No engine, sim, save schema, migration, `SAVE_VERSION`, RNG, gameplay, dependency, or product feature code changed in the PR #67 fix.

Patch 0.2 is complete: the full remote public-release gate passed on GitHub for PR #67 with 37/37 release-gate steps green. The release-gate job reported `PASS: full public-release gate completed in 5687.4s` (job runtime 1h35m7s). The main-branch CI rerun after merge also passed `test`, `determinism-gate`, and `release-gate`.

Patch 0.4 intent is satisfied through GitHub branch protection on `main`. Protection now requires status checks `test` and `determinism-gate`, requires branches to be up to date before merging (`strict: true`), enforces protection for admins, disallows force pushes, and disallows deletions. `release-gate` is intentionally not required yet because it is too slow/new to block every merge. Required linear history is off, required PR reviews are not configured, and branch restrictions are not configured.

The GitHub Pages deploy for `89c077f95634b2bf2b265f6757ddac692139d075` initially built successfully but failed twice inside `actions/deploy-pages@v4` after the deployment reached `syncing_files` with the platform message `Deployment failed, try again later.` A full Pages workflow rerun produced a fresh artifact and deployed successfully. Live-site verification then loaded `https://kevinbigham.github.io/MFD/` in headless Chrome and confirmed the page rendered `Mr. Football Dynasty v1.0.0` / Save v36 content with no console/runtime errors on initial load.

### CI Failure Root Causes Recorded

- Failure #1: main CI after PR #66 ran `scripts/__tests__/grade-season.test.ts` through plain Node test, which could not execute the TypeScript file extension.
- Failure #2: the first PR #67 release-gate run hit the old 75-minute job timeout before the full 37-step public-release gate could finish.
- Failure #3: the next release-gate run used Node 20 for browser smokes; the G1/G2 smoke required a runtime with built-in `fetch` and `WebSocket`, so Node 24 was required.
- Failure #4: the G1/G2 full-setup smoke timed out waiting for the preview server because the harness did not detect preview child signal/error exits, went through a brittle `pnpm preview` layer, and still contained stale full-setup copy assertions. The fix added local Vite preference, preview diagnostics, signal/error detection, a separate preview timeout, and source-verified copy assertions.
- Failure #5: GitHub Pages deploy accepted the artifact and created the deployment, then failed during `syncing_files` with a GitHub Pages service-side `try again later` error. A full workflow rerun with a fresh artifact succeeded; no deploy-workflow restructure was made.

### Verification

- PR #67 GitHub checks: `determinism-gate` passed in 24s; `test` passed in 33m29s; `release-gate` passed in 1h35m7s with 37/37 steps and 5687.4s full-gate script runtime.
- Main CI after PR #67: `determinism-gate`, `test`, and `release-gate` passed for `89c077f95634b2bf2b265f6757ddac692139d075`.
- GitHub Pages after PR #67: fresh workflow rerun passed build and deploy; live site rendered with no console/runtime errors on initial load.
- Branch protection readback confirmed `strict: true`, contexts `test` and `determinism-gate`, `enforce_admins: true`, `allow_force_pushes: false`, and `allow_deletions: false`.

### Checks Not Run

- No additional product tests were run for this ledger-only update. This branch changes documentation only.

### Rollback

Revert this `STATUS.md` ledger entry only. Do not roll back PR #66, PR #67, branch protection, or the successful Pages deployment unless Director separately requests that operational rollback.

## Run Ledger - 2026-07-06 GOAT Director Patch 3.1 Team Window Read-Model

Implemented Patch 3.1 — Team window read-model. `computeTeamWindow` is a web-only deterministic read-model that classifies CPU clubs as `ALL_IN`, `CONTEND`, `RETOOL`, or `REBUILD`, with `clear` or `mixed` confidence and 2-4 receipted drivers. The rubric reads only already-saved or render-derived inputs: roster/QB/core age and OVR, current cap space, draft-pick inventory, saved `team.gmStrategy`, saved `team.philosophy`, current record, team-needs cap flexibility, and saved `game.franchiseHistory`.

`/team-needs` now shows the selected CPU comparison team's competitive-window badge and driver panel beside the existing CPU Intent ledger. Trade Finder rows on `/trades` now show compact partner window badges with expandable driver text. The feature explains CPU teams only; it does not alter CPU strategy, offers, bids, trades, draft logic, team-needs refresh behavior, save data, schema, migrations, `SAVE_VERSION`, sim math, RNG channels, dependencies, CI/deploy wiring, or engine source.

## Run Ledger - 2026-07-06 GOAT Director Patch 1.3 Previously-On Session Opener

Implemented Patch 1.3 — Previously-on session opener. `buildSessionRecap` derives a max-three-beat returning-player recap from already-saved week summaries, league news, standings context, next opponent, and existing high-priority pending items. Brand-new or sparse saves return `null`, missing optional inputs are treated as empty, and recap content is deterministic for a given save.

Monday Briefing now decides visibility through browser-local convenience state only: `mfd.sessionRecap.lastSeen.v1:<dynastyId>` stores `{ dynastyId, timestamp }`, stale after three days by default, isolated per dynasty, and suppressed for the current browser session after display or dismiss. Chip presents the recap when `VITE_CHIP_ENABLED` is active; otherwise the route falls back to a dismissible Pixel banner. No `GameState` shape, save schema, migrations, `SAVE_VERSION`, sim math, RNG channels, week-advance rules, dependencies, CI/deploy wiring, or engine source changed.

## Run Ledger - 2026-06-23 G6 Setup Chip Scroll-Target Clearance Split

Fixed the reported opening Assistant GM setup screen where the enlarged Chip rail could scroll to `Where` but would not let that row settle cleanly above the bottom action bar. The issue was that the setup scroll containers used the same large value for physical command-bar padding and `scroll-padding-bottom`; at the 756px-wide in-app viewport, that made `scrollIntoView` place the `Where` row at the top edge of a 330px scrollport. The setup shell and embedded AGM rail now keep large bottom padding for the fixed command bar, but use smaller scroll-target clearances so Chip rows and `not now Chip!` land in the readable viewport. Saves, migrations, RNG behavior, formulas, gameplay rules, dependencies, route registration, action availability, setup decisions, week-advance behavior, and `SAVE_VERSION` are unchanged.

### Failed Attempts / Fixes

- The first full release run failed at `playtest-all`: every persona had 30 high-severity `cap-sanity` anomalies after the first offseason because the synthetic harness roster contracts exceeded the fixture's hard-coded cap totals. The fix was source-level fixture truth, not weakening assertions.
- The first shadow compare after that fix failed because all three frozen reports legitimately drifted. The diff was classified as intended, the corpus was bumped to v2 with metadata reason/citation, and compare mode then passed.
- The generic web test step originally duplicated the long G4 soak and looked hung. The release runner now excludes `src/app/store/g4-multi-year-trust.test.ts` from generic web tests and runs it through the dedicated G4 step.

### Checks Not Run

- A GitHub Actions workflow was not added or run; G7 is green through the local repeatable release command.
- `pnpm` was not run because this shell has no `pnpm` binary on `PATH`; package-local binaries and Node were used.
- `git status` was not run because this extracted checkout has no `.git` directory.
- Screenshot/image-diff review was not added beyond the existing DOM visual/playability and zero-console browser sweeps.

### Residual Risk

- The full release gate is long by design: playtest, shadow, and G4 account for most runtime.
- `speedrunner-20y` shadow still records known high-severity anomalies in the 800-step truncated corpus; it remains a frozen drift detector, not a clean 20-season proof.
- The command is local automation. CI can wire the same command later, but release readiness no longer depends on remembering separate manual commands.

### Rollback

Remove `release:gate` from `package.json`, delete `scripts/release-gate.mjs` and `scripts/__tests__/release-gate.test.mjs`, revert the playtest harness cap-fixture changes and shadow corpus v2 files, then restore the prior focused test expectations. No save schema, `SAVE_VERSION`, migration, route registration, user save data, or production dependency rollback is required.

### Best Next Slice

With G1-G7 green, next work should be release packaging/CI wiring, changelog/version/public-page polish, or post-release hardening. Do not reopen gate work unless a source change invalidates the full `node scripts/release-gate.mjs` evidence.

Persisted team `gmStrategy` values now normalize to the public `GM_STRATEGIES` catalog at the engine save boundary: legacy `buy` / `buyer` become `contend`, legacy `sell` / `seller` become `rebuild`, and malformed or missing values become `neutral`. This protects current-version cartridge imports and old-save migrations without calling `applyGmStrategy`, rewriting roster `tradeBlock` flags, bumping `SAVE_VERSION`, or changing sim/RNG/movement behavior.

- `packages/engine/src/systems/gm-strategies.ts`

- `CODEX_GOAT_MARATHON_PROMPT.md`

- `STATUS.md`

### What Changed

- Added engine-owned `normalizeGmStrategy(value)` for canonical CPU strategy ids.
- Made `TeamPersistedSchema` name and normalize `gmStrategy` instead of passing arbitrary values through uninspected.
- Updated the v35->v36 migration to normalize team GM strategies for old-save imports that pass through the migration chain.
- Kept normalization separate from `applyGmStrategy`, so imported saves do not implicitly recompute CPU trade-block flags.
- Added focused engine save/migration/schema tests and a web cartridge-import test for current-version imports carrying legacy strategy values.
